## Adaptive‑Learning Platform: **Global Core + Local Shell** **Target Markets:** Vietnam (Asia), Saudi Arabia (Middle East), France (Europe), Kenya (East Africa) **Launch Year:** 2026 (funnel-ready by Q1‑2027) --- ### 1. Strategic Vision > **Build a “Core+Shell” system** that preserves our US‑based adaptive‑learning engine (AI grading, data analytics, UX, security) while the *Shell* is country‑specific in curricula, pedagogy, language, legal compliance, and sales channels. > - **Goal:** 1 million active learners across the four markets by year 3, with > 90 % adoption reported by school authorities or parents. > - **KPIs:** > - **Curricular coverage** (≥ 80 % of mandated learning outcomes). > - **User engagement** (avg. 1 hr/day / learner). > - **Retention** (≥ 85 % of students continue past the 1st semester). > - **Monetization mix:** > 45 % govt‑procurement / > 40 % direct‑to‑consumer (parental subscriptions) by year 3. --- ### 2. Market‑by‑Market Snapshot | Country | Curriculum Mandate | Language of Instruction | Screen‑time Culture | Standardized Tests | Procurement | Main Pain‑point for Tech Provider | |---------|--------------------|------------------------|---------------------|--------------------|-------------|----------------------------------| | **Vietnam** | 12‑year K‑12 system. National exams (HSG – High School Graduation) have full coverage of math, literature, sciences. | Vietnamese (official), English for higher education. | *High* (parents accept screens as “modern”), but school tech budgets are limited. | HSG; B3 (for higher ed entrants). | Mainly *direct‑to‑consumer* via school consortia or individual; some pilot govt pilots. | Need to fit content to a *single‑language* environment, high‑mobile usage. | | **Saudi Arabia** | Al‑Qudra (national curriculum), strong emphasis on Arabic and Islamic studies. | Arabic (mandatory), English secondary. | Moderate–High: school policy limits > 1 hr/day; 2024 “Digital Learning Initiative” requires balance. | “Al‑Taqasim” national tests yearly. | Heavy *government procurement* through Ministry of Education; private schools can buy directly. | Must satisfy halal‑audit, Arabic UI, embed Qur’an content & ethics. | | **France** | Programme national (cycle 1–3). Strong focus on literacy, maths, science, French, history‑geography. | French (official). | Low: strict regulation of screen use in primary schools, 60‑min/day caps. | National diploma (CAP, Baccalauréat). | Predominantly *public procurement* through ministries, regional boards, “Projet Digital” programs. | Must integrate *pedagogical rigor*, respect “conservez-vous à la pédagogie critique” ethos. | | **Kenya** | National Curriculum Framework (NCF) K‑12; English & Swahili taught. | Bilingual (English & Swahili). | Moderate: parents highly value technology but also value human interaction. | KCSE (Kenyan Certificate of Secondary Education). | Mix of *public procurement* (primary/secondary) and *private schools* subscription. | Needs low‑bandwidth performance, Swahili localisation, partnership with E‑diploma regulators. | --- ### 3. Core‑Technology Architecture | Layer | Rationale | Key Features | |-------|-----------|--------------| | **Adaptive Engine** | AI‑driven pacing, knowledge‑gap analytics, micro‑learning suggestions. | Open‑API, pluggable modules for content, language‑model, evaluation. | | **Learning Management System (LMS) Front‑end** | Uniform UX for all markets – adjustable styling. | Responsive, offline caching, multi‑device sync, universal login. | | **CMS (Content API)** | Separate content layer that pulls from the UK / US library. | Tag‑based metadata (subject, grade, language, exam‑align). | | **Compliance & Data‑Governance** | GDPR, COPPA, local data‑shelter laws. | Role‑based data residency, encryption, audit logs. | | **Analytics & Reporting** | Real‑time dashboards for teachers, parents, administrators. | Customizable reports aligned with local exam rubric. | *All core code remains in the US data center, but we will introduce a **Regional Mirror** (EU‑EU, Middle‑East, Asia‑Pacific, Africa) to reduce latency and meet data‑shelter mandates.* --- ### 4. Localization “Shell” – What Changes? | Component | Vietnam | Saudi Arabia | France | Kenya | |-----------|---------|--------------|--------|-------| | **Curricular Mapping** | Map to 12‑year NDP units + HSG outcomes | Map to Al‑Qudra 4-year cycle + Al‑Taqasim | Map to Cycle 1‑3; Baccalauréat subjects | NCF K‑12; KCSE core tests | | **Language** | Vietnamese UI, English bilingual | Arabic UI + English options | French UI + English (optional) | Swahili UI + English | | **Assessment Strategy** | Mix of formative quizzes + HSG‑aligned summative tests | Halal‑approved assessment templates; avoid high‑stakes in primary | Focus on formative + “Centrée sur la compréhension” | KCSE simulation tests, formative quizzes | | **Screen‑time Controls** | In‑app screen‑time tracker + parental dashboard; push alerts for 1‑hr limits | Built‑in hour‑caps (configurable per school) | Strict 60‑min/day rule; offline mode; “study‑time” indicator | Adaptive “study‑time” + optional screen‑time coach | | **Pedagogical Framing** | Gamified lessons, micro‑learning, group play | Respect Quranic value; integrate religious life‑skills | Inquiry‑based, teacher‑guided, no “learning through play” emphasis | Community‑based projects, blended with local NGOs | | **Regulatory Compliance** | Ensure content is “free of politically incorrect content” | Halal‑audit; no secular or conflicting narratives | “Respect the French educational ethos”; avoid political bias | Ensure no copyright infringement; local content approvals | | **Payment & Procurement** | Parent purchases via UPI / mobile wallet; school consortia via bulk | Ministry of Education digital‑procurement; private via e‑commerce | Public procurement via central e‑Sourcing, with local vendor integration | Mixed: school‑direct, ministry digital tender, NGO co‑financing | > **Key Takeaway:** The *Curricular, Lang, & Regulatory* layers demand a full “Shell”, whereas the *Adaptive Engine* remains untouched. --- ### 5. Content Strategy 1. **Core US Library (English‑only)** – 10 × 10 K lessons across STEM, ESL, Social‑Sciences. 2. **Local Author Network** – 70 % new content sourced from local teachers (grant‑based). 3. **Translation & Localization** – Machine‑translation + human QA; 90 % localization cost. 4. **Assessment Bank Alignment** – 200+ practice tests per curriculum unit with analytics for scoring rubrics. 5. **Content Governance** – 2‑tier review: local teacher review panel + compliance guard. 6. **Open‑Source “Curriculum‑Sync Engine”** – Export/import JSON; fosters school‑specific custom modules. **Content Creation Workflow** | Step | Responsible | Outcome | |------|--------------|---------| | 1. Curriculum mapping | Local curriculum experts | Mapping matrix (subject→lesson→outcome) | | 2. Author training | In‑house instructional design team | Standardised lesson templates | | 3. Draft writing | Local content authors | Lesson draft, quiz questions | | 4. Peer review | Teacher consortium | Subject‑matter validation | | 5. Translation | Linguist + native speaker | Multi‑lingual asset | | 6. Compliance audit | Legal + local regulators | Certification badge | | 7. Upload & QA | CMS operations | Live in‑app lesson | --- ### 6. Engagement & User Experience | Market | Primary Users | Engagement Touch‑points | Parental Attitudes | |--------|---------------|------------------------|-------------------| | **Vietnam** | Parents & mobile‑first elementary | Mobile‑first UI, push notifications | Accept screens; want academic progress | | **Saudi Arabia** | Teachers, parents in private schools | Teacher portal, parent portal, Al‑Qudra dashboards | Concern over screen time, value “halal” content | | **France** | Teachers & inspectors | Integrated school dashboard, offline mode | Strict on-screen usage; desire pedagogy that fosters reasoning | | **Kenya** | Primary/secondary students | Audio‑focussed, low‑bandwidth mode, community leaderboards | Parents value affordability, community acceptance | **Universal Design** - **Accessibility** (closed captions, high‑contrast UI). - **Offline mode** (progress sync when connected). - **Gamification** (only to the extent allowed by local policy). - **Analytics** (teacher dashboards, parent progress). --- ### 7. Pricing & Monetization Model | Channel | Price Model | Typical Cost | Adoption Incentives | |---------|--------------|--------------|--------------------| | **Government procurement** | Tiered institutional licensing | 50 k USD per school (per annum) | “Digital Learning Grants” (ex. France’s “Projet Digital 2025”) | | **Private schools** | Per‑student subscription | 20 USD/month per student | Volume discount, “early‑adopter” grant | | **Mass‑market (home‑learning)** | Direct‑to‑consumer consumer app | 5 USD/month per learner | Free trial (1 month), family plan | | **Hybrid Ed‑Tech partners** | Revenue‑share | 30 % of revenue | Integration with local e‑diploma systems | **Cost‑sharing Examples** - **Vietnam:** MOE can subsidise up to 70 % for public schools; private schools pay full price. - **Saudi:** Ministry can provide “E‑Learning” vouchers; partnership with local media for teacher training. - **France:** Public schools must meet *“Accréditation pédagogique”*; partner with UNESCO‑France for grant. - **Kenya:** MOH & Ministry of Education joint procurement; local NGOs fund initial 5 % discount. --- ### 8. Procurement & Partnership Road‑Map | Q | Activity | Owner | |---|----------|-------| | 0–12 | **Legal/Compliance Fast‑Track** – Data‑shelter, halal audit, French pedagogy review | Regional Legal Counsel | | 1–6 | **Pilot Schools** – 5 schools per country (1 per curriculum level), 200 students | Sales & Implementation | | 6–12 | **Government Tender Response** – Build e‑proposals, case studies, ROI docs | Commercial & Technical | | 6–18 | **Teacher Ambassadors** – 50 teachers per country, curriculum champions | Partner Ops | | 12–24 | **Scale‑Up** – On‑boarding 200 schools per country, regional rollout | Ops | **Key Partnerships** - **Vietnam:** Ministry of Education & Training + local tech incubators. - **Saudi:** Ministry of Education & King Abdulaziz City for Science & Technology. - **France:** Ministry of Elementary Education + Digital Learning Hub. - **Kenya:** Ministry of Education & UNESCO Kenya. --- ### 9. Compliance & Governance | Country | Governing Body | Key Compliance Points | Required Documentation | |---------|----------------|----------------------|------------------------| | Vietnam | MOET | Data residency, content approval for exams | Content approval dossier | | Saudi | MoE, Ministry of Justice | Halal‑certified content, Arabic localization, data sovereignty | Halal audit, Arabic UI, local data centre lease | | France | Ministry of Education, CNIL | GDPR, “Bourse d’Apprentissage” audits | Data processing agreement, educational audit report | | Kenya | Ministry of Education, Data Protection | Data localisation (10 % storage in Kenya), exam compliance | Localization certificate, exam‑aligned curriculum map | **Risk Mitigation** | Risk | Mitigation | Backup Plan | |------|------------|-------------| | Regulatory delays | Continuous liaison, pre‑approval “white‑papers” | Dual‑launch: start with private schools (less hurdles) | | Teacher resistance | Free teacher training, local content authors | Build a “Teacher Advisory Board” to co‑design | | Funding gaps | Tiered pricing, grant‑applications | Strategic alliances with NGOs | --- ### 10. Technology Road‑Map (3 Years) | Stage | Goals | Deliverables | |-------|-------|--------------| | **Phase 1 (0‑9 mo)** | Build Core + Regional Mirroring | • Adaptive Engine release v2.0
• L2‑regional data centers (EU, AP‑Asia, MENA, AFR).
• Content API ready for 5 languages. | | **Phase 2 (9‑18 mo)** | Launch Pilot pilots | • 5 schools per market
• Teacher training modules
• In‑app analytics dashboards | | **Phase 3 (18‑30 mo)** | Scale & Institutionalized procurement | • Gov. tender wins
• 200 schools/month in each market
• 1 M active learners by year 3 | | **Phase 4 (30‑36 mo)** | R&D for AI‑in‑assessment & cross‑curriculum analytics | • AI‑assessment engine
• Data‑driven personalised growth plans | --- ### 11. Success Metrics by Country (Year 3) | Market | Core Adoption | Curriculum Coverage | Screen‑time Adherence | Teacher Satisfaction | |--------|---------------|---------------------|-----------------------|----------------------| | Vietnam | 70 k learners, 80 % schools | 92 % alignment to HSG | < 1 hr/day for > 60 % students | Avg. 4.5/5 | | Saudi | 100 k learners → 500 schools | 95 % alignment to Al‑Qudra | 90 % adherence to hour‑caps | Avg. 4.7/5 | | France | 40 k learners → 200 schools | 90 % alignment to Baccalauréat | 80 % compliance | Avg. 4.0/5 (per policy) | | Kenya | 120 k learners → 600 schools | 93 % alignment to KCSE | 70 % adherence | Avg. 4.3/5 | --- ## Final Recommendations (Executive Summary) 1. **Invest in a “Core+Shell” Architecture** – Keep the core adaptive engine globally unified; implement per‑market SDKs for curriculum, language, and compliance. 2. **Prioritize Regulatory Pre‑Clearance** – Launch legal teams in each country 12 months early; obtain “Halal‑audit” and “French Pedagogy Certification” before product rollout. 3. **Build a Dual‑Channel Sales Engine** – One directed at ministries (public procurement) and one for private schools/parents (subscription & micro‑learning). 4. **Cultivate Local Author Communities** – 70 % of content should be locally produced; use government grant programs to support author incentives. 5. **Implement Robust Analytics & Dashboards** – Align with national exam rubrics; enable teachers to see “learning gaps” and “screen‑time trends”. 6. **Launch in Phased Pilots** – Start with 5 pilot schools per market, gather data, refine the “Shell”, then ramp up procurement. 7. **Allocate 30‑% of Budget to Localization, 70 % to Tech & Data Security** – The biggest win comes from a culturally attuned product, not a fancy tech showcase. 8. **Create a “Cross‑Market Insight Hub”** – Use data from all four countries to continuously improve the core engine (e.g., universal adaptive algorithms, advanced NLP for local languages). By executing this balanced, country‑centric strategy, the startup can successfully navigate the complex regulatory landscapes, meet divergent learner needs, and create a profitable, sustainable adaptive‑learning ecosystem across Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, France, and Kenya.
